title: How to Find Your Perfect Heel Height — A Comfort Guide for Nairobi Women
excerpt: Not every occasion needs 4 inches. Here's how to pick a heel height that matches your day, your outfit, and your feet — without sacrificing the glam.
content:
Let's have an honest conversation, pair to pair: not every occasion calls for your tallest stiletto, and choosing the right heel height is half the battle between "I own this room" and "I cannot feel my toes." At The Tinnsrack, we get asked about heel height almost as often as we get asked about size — so here's the guide we wish someone had handed us years ago.

Start with the day, not the shoe

Before you fall for a pair on the shelf, think about what you'll actually be doing in them. Standing at a wedding reception for six hours is a different mission from a seated dinner at a rooftop restaurant. A heel that photographs beautifully for twenty minutes isn't always the one that gets you home happy at midnight.

The low heel — 3 to 5cm

This is your everyday workhorse. Kitten heels and low block heels in this range give you lift and posture without the strain, which makes them ideal for the office, running errands around town, or a casual lunch date. They're also the easiest height to walk confidently in from the first wear, no breaking-in period required.

The mid heel — 6 to 8cm

Our most versatile zone, and where a lot of our mules and block heels live. This height elevates an outfit without demanding your full attention to stay upright, which makes it the sweet spot for office parties, date nights, and the kind of "just dressy enough" events that fill a Nairobi social calendar. Think of it as your default setting for looking put-together.

The high heel — 8.5cm and up

This is drama, and drama is exactly what a wedding, a graduation, or a big night out calls for. Our stiletto mules and pointed pumps in this range are built for moments, not marathons — so pair them with occasions where you'll be sitting more than you're sprinting between matatu stages.

Our honest advice

If you're torn between two heights, go lower. A comfortable 6cm heel worn all night beats a stunning 10cm heel abandoned under the table by 9pm. And if you're ever unsure what height suits your event, call or WhatsApp us at 0768 008 365 — we'll talk you through it like we would a friend standing right there in the shop with us.

However tall you go, remember: confidence is the real heel height. Everything else is just the shoe underneath it.

A quick height cheat sheet

If you're standing in front of your wardrobe with fifteen minutes to decide, here's the shortcut version: office day, low heel. Dinner or date night, mid heel. Wedding, graduation, or big night out, go as high as you're comfortable holding for a few hours. And if the event spans several of those moods in one day — a wedding that runs from church to garden reception to dance floor — the mid heel is almost always your safest, most versatile bet.

Listen to your own feet, not the trend

Every foot is different, and what feels effortless for one woman can feel like punishment for another, even in the exact same shoe. Arch height, width, and simply how much walking you're used to in heels all play a part. Don't be talked into a height that doesn't suit you just because it's what's trending on Instagram this month — the most stylish shoe in the room is always the one you're wearing with ease, not the one you're quietly suffering through.

title: Heels vs Wedges vs Sandals — Choosing the Right Shoe for the Occasion
excerpt: Three silhouettes, three very different jobs. Here's how to know which one your outfit — and your day — actually needs.
content:
Every pair in our shop has a job to do, and knowing which silhouette fits which occasion saves you the "why did I wear this" regret before you've even left the house. Let's break down the three shapes we get asked about most.

Heels — for the moments that matter

Stilettos, pumps, and heeled mules are your statement-makers. They're sharp, they're polished, and they carry a room the moment you walk into it. Reach for heels when the occasion is formal, celebratory, or simply deserves your full effort — a wedding, a graduation, an office party where you want to be remembered. The trade-off is comfort over long stretches, so save them for events with more standing-still than standing-around.

Wedges — for comfort with attitude

A wedge gives you height and stability in one move, since the weight is distributed across the whole sole rather than balanced on a thin point. This makes wedges the smarter choice for events on grass, gravel, or uneven ground — think outdoor functions, garden weddings, or a long day of running around Nairobi without switching shoes at lunch. They're also forgiving for anyone newer to heels, or simply not in the mood to negotiate with a stiletto today.

Sandals — for everyday ease

Open, breathable, and unfussy, sandals are your go-to for the Nairobi heat, casual weekend plans, or an occasion where "dressy" isn't really the assignment. A low-heeled sandal still elevates an outfit, just without asking much of your feet in return. They're the shoe you can wear from a coffee run straight into an impromptu afternoon plan.

So, which one do you actually need?

Ask yourself three things: how long will I be on my feet, what's the ground like, and how formal is the mood? A quick mental checklist beats a regretful 9pm foot-swap into flats every time. And if you're still torn between two pairs, that's exactly what we're here for — WhatsApp us a description of your event and we'll point you to the right one.

The right silhouette doesn't just complete an outfit. It lets you actually enjoy wearing it.

Mixing and matching across a single day

Plenty of Nairobi days aren't just one occasion — you might start with a work meeting, move into a lunch celebration, and end at a friend's send-off, all in the same eight hours. Rather than trying to find one shoe that does everything, consider packing a lightweight backup in your bag. A block heel in the morning, swapped for a sandal by evening, saves your feet without sacrificing how put-together you look at any single stop.

Colour and material change the equation too

Beyond the silhouette itself, think about how colour and finish shift the formality of each shape. A black satin heel reads formal almost anywhere, while the same heel shape in a bright ombré or metallic finish leans party. A neutral tan wedge feels casual, while a gold or embellished wedge can hold its own at a dressier outdoor event. When you're deciding, silhouette answers "how practical," and colour answers "how dressed up" — together, they tell you exactly what the shoe is really saying.

title: Wedding Guest Shoe Guide — What to Wear to Every Kenyan Wedding This Season
excerpt: Church ceremony, outdoor garden reception, or a full traditional send-off — your shoes should be ready for all of it. Here's how to get it right.
content:
Wedding season in Kenya moves fast — sometimes two invitations in one weekend — and your shoe choice has to keep up with venues that shift from church pew to garden lawn to dance floor, often on the very same day. Here's our pair-by-pair breakdown for getting it right, every time.

The church ceremony

You'll mostly be seated, which means this is your moment to go as elegant as you like. A satin heeled mule or a pointed stiletto pump in a rich jewel tone or classic black photographs beautifully and pairs effortlessly with structured, formal fits. Comfort still matters for the walk in and out, so make sure the fit is snug, not just striking.

The garden or outdoor reception

This is where a wedge earns its keep. Soft ground and heel-eating gravel are no match for a stable wedge sole, and you'll thank yourself later for not sinking three inches into a lawn mid-photo. A block heel works nearly as well if wedges aren't your style — just avoid anything with a thin stiletto point for this leg of the day.

The reception dinner and speeches

Back to seated territory, so this is your excuse to switch into (or stay in) your dressiest pair. A mid-to-high heel in gold, blush, or a bold ombré shade adds polish for photos with the couple and pairs beautifully with an evening gown or a fitted dress.

The send-off and dance floor

Honest talk: this is when most of us regret our shoe choice. If you know you're staying until the dance floor opens, bring a lower block heel or comfortable pump as a backup, or choose one versatile mid-heel pair for the entire day rather than switching. Your feet — and your Instagram stories — will both be grateful.

Our wedding-guest go-tos

For most Kenyan weddings, we point guests toward a satin mule or block-heel pump in the 6–8cm range: dressy enough for photos, stable enough for a full day of standing, sitting, and dancing. Need help matching a pair to your outfit? Send us a photo on WhatsApp and we'll style it with you.

Whichever pair you choose, remember: you're not just dressing for the ceremony, you're dressing for the whole day. Choose accordingly, and step out looking every bit the guest of honour.

What to pack as backup

Even the best-planned shoe choice can meet an unexpected grass patch, an extra-long queue for photos, or a reception that runs later than promised. A small, foldable flat tucked into your handbag is the quiet insurance policy every seasoned wedding guest carries — not because you'll definitely need it, but because knowing it's there lets you enjoy the whole day without watching the clock on your feet.

Traditional ceremonies and send-offs

Kenyan weddings often include a traditional segment — a ruracio, a send-off, or a cultural ceremony — that may take place on grass, in a compound, or somewhere with more uneven footing than a church aisle. For these moments, prioritise stability over height. A wedge or a lower block heel lets you move naturally through the celebration, dance if the moment calls for it, and avoid the very specific stress of a heel sinking into soft ground mid-photo.

title: How to Make Heels Comfortable for an All-Day Event
excerpt: You don't have to choose between looking good and feeling good. A few small habits make the difference between a great day and a painful one.
content:
"Beautiful but painful" doesn't have to be the deal you make every time you wear heels. A little preparation goes a long way, and most of the discomfort people associate with heels actually comes down to a few fixable habits — not the shoes themselves.

Break them in before the big day

Never wear a brand-new pair for the first time to an all-day event. Walk around the house in them for short stretches over a few days beforehand so the material softens slightly and you learn exactly how they move with your stride. Satin and leather both give a little with wear — but only if you let them.

Size matters more than you think

A heel that's even half a size too small will hurt within the hour, no matter how well it's made. If you're between sizes, size up rather than down — a slightly loose fit is far more fixable (with an insole or heel grip) than a tight one. Not sure of your size? Call or WhatsApp us at 0768 008 365 before you order and we'll help you get it right the first time.

Cushion the pressure points

The ball of your foot takes the brunt of the impact in most heels, especially stilettos. A gel forefoot cushion or a simple insole insert redistributes that pressure and can genuinely double your comfortable wear-time. It's a small investment that pays off every single time you wear the shoe.

Give your feet micro-breaks

Whenever you get a seated moment — during speeches, in the car, waiting for photos — slip your heels off for even sixty seconds and flex your feet. This tiny reset prevents the cumulative ache that builds up over a full day and makes the final stretch of the event so much more bearable.

Choose the right height for the day

We say this often because it's the biggest lever you have: a well-fitted 6cm heel worn comfortably all day will always look better in photos than a stunning 10cm heel you're visibly wincing in by evening. Match the height to how long you'll actually be standing.

Comfort and glamour aren't opposites — they just take a little planning. Get the fit, the height, and the prep right, and your heels will carry you through the whole event, not just the entrance.

Pay attention to the strap

A secure ankle or T-strap does more for your comfort than most people realise — it keeps your foot from sliding forward with every step, which is usually the real cause of pinched toes by the end of the night. If you're choosing between two similar pairs, the one with a proper strap will almost always carry you further.

Don't underestimate the surface you'll be walking on

Tile, gravel, grass, and carpet all demand different things from a heel. A thin stiletto tip that glides across a polished hotel floor can sink straight into a lawn or catch on uneven paving outside a church. Where you know the venue in advance, match your heel width to the ground — and where you don't, a slightly wider heel base is the safer, comfort-first choice.

title: The Tinnsrack Guide to Building a Shoe Wardrobe That Works for Everything
excerpt: You don't need thirty pairs. You need the right five. Here's how to build a shoe collection that covers every occasion on your calendar.
content:
Here's a little secret from the shop floor: the women who always seem to have "the perfect pair" for every occasion usually don't own the most shoes — they own the right ones. A tightly curated collection beats a crowded closet every time. Here's how we'd build yours.

1. The reliable black heel

Non-negotiable, and the hardest-working pair you'll own. A black mule or pump in a mid heel height goes with nearly everything in your wardrobe and works for the office, dinner, and most formal occasions. If you only buy one pair this year, make it this one.

2. The neutral everyday flat or low sandal

For the days heels simply aren't the plan. A nude or tan low sandal quietly elongates the leg while keeping you comfortable enough for a full day on your feet — errands, casual lunches, travel days.

3. The statement heel

This is where you get to have fun — a bold colour, a rhinestone bow, an ombré fade, a metallic finish. Every wardrobe needs one pair that isn't trying to be practical, just unforgettable. Save it for the events where you actually want to be the one people remember.

4. The wedge or block heel for movement

Garden parties, long events, or days you know you'll be on your feet for hours all call for stability. A wedge or block heel in a versatile colour like black or tan handles all of it without complaint.

5. The occasion pair you're still missing

Think honestly about what your calendar actually looks like. Attending a lot of weddings this season? A satin mule in blush or gold earns its keep fast. More office events than parties? A sleek kitten heel might be your real gap.

Quality over quantity, always

Five well-chosen pairs that you reach for constantly will always outperform fifteen impulse buys gathering dust. Next time you're browsing, ask yourself: does this fill a real gap, or am I just falling for the shine? (No judgment either way — sometimes the shine wins, and that's allowed too.)

Not sure what your collection is missing? Come see us at Shop F17, Beba Beba, or drop us a message — we love nothing more than helping a woman build a shoe wardrobe that actually works for her life.

Auditing what you already own

Before your next purchase, try a quick closet audit. Pull every pair out and sort them by how often you've actually worn each one in the last six months. You'll usually find the same two or three pairs doing all the work, while several others sit untouched. That's not a failure — it's useful information. It tells you exactly which category deserves your next investment, and which categories you can happily skip for now.

Buy for your actual life, not your aspirational one

It's easy to fall for a towering evening heel because it looks stunning on the shelf, even if your calendar is mostly office days and casual weekends. The best-built wardrobes reflect the life you're actually living, not the one you occasionally imagine. Be honest about your week, and let that honesty guide what earns a spot in your collection.

title: How to Care for Satin and Suede Shoes — Keep Them Looking New
excerpt: Delicate materials deserve a little extra care. Here's how to keep your satin and suede pairs looking as good as the day you bought them.
content:
Satin and suede are two of our favourite materials to sell — and also two of the most delicate. A little care goes a long way toward keeping that just-bought shine for years, not just one season. Here's how we look after our own pairs.

Storage is step one

Always store your shoes in a cool, dry place, away from direct sunlight, which can fade satin's sheen and dry out leather soles over time. If you kept the box or a dust bag, use it — it protects against dust and keeps the shape of the shoe intact between wears.

Caring for satin

Satin is a fabric first, so treat it a little like your favourite dress. Wipe away everyday dust or light marks with a soft, dry cloth, working gently in one direction rather than scrubbing. For anything more than surface dust, avoid water altogether — satin can water-mark easily — and instead take it to a professional cleaner who works with delicate fabrics.

Caring for suede

Suede needs a dedicated suede brush, not a cloth. Brush in short strokes to lift dust and restore the nap, and always let suede air dry naturally if it gets damp — never near direct heat, which can crack and stiffen the material. A suede protector spray applied before first wear also makes a real difference in how the material handles Nairobi's dust and the occasional surprise downpour.

The golden rule for both

Avoid prolonged exposure to water. A sudden rain shower happens to the best of us, but if it happens to your satin or suede pair, let them air dry naturally away from heat and resist the urge to force them dry — patience preserves the material far better than a heater or hairdryer ever will.

When in doubt, ask us

If a pair from us ever needs a little TLC and you're not sure how to approach it, WhatsApp us a photo — we've handled enough satin and suede over the years to usually have a straightforward answer.

Treat your shoes well, and they'll return the favour for a long time. A little care today means many more nights out in the pair you love.

A simple after-wear routine

Make it a habit to give your shoes two minutes of attention as soon as you take them off, rather than tossing them straight into the closet. Wipe away any visible dust or marks, let them air out fully before storing, and check the soles for any debris picked up during the day. This small routine, done consistently, does more for a shoe's lifespan than any occasional deep clean ever will.

Protecting new pairs from day one

If you can, treat satin and suede pairs with a protective spray before their very first wear, not after the first scuff. A light, even coat creates a barrier against dust, light rain, and everyday marks, and takes only a few minutes to apply. It's a small step at the start that saves you a much bigger headache later.
